P1.evidence: The setter call was acknowledged but nothing from it was played back - 'I already saw a few things coming by from Derek. already spoke to him about everything.' The frame reached three of four parts, including a gesture at the gap: 'where you're at, where you want to go, see if we can really help you bridge that gap.' Frame agreement was taken. The open question was never asked - the prospect simply started talking after 'Sounds good?' and the rep let him run.

P2.evidence: Occupation was asked directly and the desk-bound problem properly explored. The injury check ran and produced the central fact of the call - no ACL in either knee - with cause and functional impact both followed up. Activity was quantified well, in steps per day now versus in the field. Nutrition was thorough, including the home-versus-away split and off-script frequency. But age, height and weight were all volunteered rather than asked, health conditions were never raised, and the single most alarming disclosure on the call - losing 40 lb of muscle mass while 'doing a shot' with almost no protein intake - drew no follow-up at all. Sleep and energy were not asked.

P3.evidence: The bridge question was the best moment of the call and was asked well: 'So many people in those 72, they're like, you know what, I'm happy with this. It's not like I'm hurting too bad. Why do you think you really do want to work on this?' It produced the whole motivation in one answer - the 96-year-old father losing mobility - and the prospect later added that he wants to pass on what he learns to help his dad. What was never done was the future-state question or the reflect-back that names it: nobody said back to him that this is not about ten pounds, it is about not becoming his father. That material was sitting on the table for fifteen minutes.

P4.evidence: Past attempts were never asked for and came out unprompted - a lifetime of self-training with nobody correcting him. But the root-cause question was well put: 'What do you feel like is the reason for you to now actually be looking into doing it with someone instead of just doing it on your own again like you used to?' The prospect then named the gap himself with unusual clarity: 'you have a coach, you have intention to stay with the program. If you're doing it yourself, I don't feel like today. I'll do it tomorrow.'

P5.evidence: Never run. The consequence was handed to the rep on a plate - a father at 96 who has lost his mobility - and no version of 'what does this look like in two years if nothing changes' was ever asked. With a twenty-percent phase weight and a prospect this motivated, running it would have made the four-figure number land very differently.

P6.evidence: Ran properly and got a genuine yes before any number was mentioned: 'when you have that accountability in place, do you feel like there's anything else that would stop you from getting to the goals of losing some fat for yourself, building up more strength, also tightening up your chest and your core more?' The answer was unambiguous - 'let's make a commitment. If I'm going to make a commitment, let's do this.' Scored on process, not outcome: this phase was executed correctly and the call still ended in an argument four minutes later.

P11.evidence: Unreachable. No offer was ever presented; the prospect terminated the call as soon as a four-figure range was named.

objection_plays.detail: The money objection arrived as an ultimatum - 'if you want to charge me to do this, we can stop this right here' - and nothing from the play ran. No isolate, no SHOULD-I-versus-HOW reframe, no offer to explore making it work, no permission question, no financial picture. The rep defended the price on the grounds of Trevor's time being valuable, then argued the principle back at the prospect: 'do you feel like a personal trainer would do something for free? They have to pay their groceries as well, right?' The $1,000 Primal University tier, which this rep offered to three other prospects in the same week, was never mentioned.

A third script gap, not previously documented, and the most commercially significant one in this batch. There is no play for a prospect who has come through the entire funnel - free content, application, setter call - believing the coaching is free, and who experiences the first mention of price as a bait. 'So you did the hype. You got me here.' The script assumes price is expected and the objection is about capacity or timing. This objection was about legitimacy, and there is nothing written for it.

Clinical fit, the first documented script gap. Bilateral absent ACLs confirmed on x-ray, with swelling and weather-dependent pain, in a 72-year-old, plus a recent 40 lb loss of muscle mass on an injectable. There is no screening or clearance step, so none was run - and the rep's opening response to the disclosure was to question it: 'Do you believe that?'

notes: Everything up to minute sixteen was competent - a strong bridge question, a well-run injury check, thorough nutrition, and a clean commitment check that produced a real yes. Then the price arrived as an improvised $1,000 to $8,000 range with no presentation in front of it, and the deal did not just fail, it turned hostile. Two coaching points, but the bigger issue is not the rep's: a prospect should not reach minute sixteen of a closer call without knowing the programme costs money, and when he objects on price the rep should know whether the $1,000 tier is on the table or not.
